What do we really know about Christopher Nolan? For a filmmaker whose body of work is perhaps the most watched, and discussed, of any this century, the British blockbuster titan is still an enigma. Often, filmmakers expose the rawest and most personal parts of their psyche through their output. It’s true of someone like Steven Spielberg, whose parents’ messy divorce coloured, in different ways, more or less everything he ever made; or Martin Scorsese, whose work is all shaped and informed by his Italian Catholic upbringing. After 13 films, though, Nolan has seemed to leave us little the wiser. Or to put it in movie terms: what, exactly, is his “Rosebud”?

Nolan’s latest film, The Odyssey, might offer the clearest look yet into the mind of a man who has always resisted conventional notions of auteur analysis – though that’s not necessarily saying much. Nolan told The Hollywood Reporter back in 2015 that “the more you know about somebody who makes the films, the less you can just watch the movies”, and that he didn’t “want people to have me in mind at all when they’re watching the films”. He prefers, in other words, to let his movies do the talking. (But who can hear what they’re saying over those famously muddy sound mixes?)

Adapted from the classic Greek epic, The Odyssey stars Matt Damon as wartime hero Odysseus, making his long and arduous journey back to Ithaca, to his wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and his son Telemachus (a diligent Tom Holland, here wisely frugal with the gee-willikers credulity he oozes as Spider-Man). Throughout Nolan’s work, families have most often been significant in their absence. Dead wives abound – in Memento, The Prestige, Inception and Interstellar. In The Dark Knight trilogy, Batman’s long-dead parents are a void, with Michael Caine’s shrewd butler stepping in as surrogate father. Repeatedly, Nolan has separated fathers from their children, whether that’s through legal exile, like Leonardo DiCaprio’s Cobb in Inception, or decades-long space exploration, like Matthew McConaughey’s Cooper in Interstellar. In this way, The Odyssey is iterating on a story that Nolan has told several times before.

And yet, what this is saying about Nolan’s psyche is less clear. It’s widely speculated that filmmakers such as Wes Anderson or Paul Thomas Anderson have fixated on troubled parental relationships in their work – on so-called “bad dads” – as a way of exploring their own fraught childhoods. Thanks to his reluctance to speak about his personal life in interviews, we know little of Nolan’s childhood, but what we do know doesn’t suggest some kind of traumatic origin story. His mother Christine is an American, a former flight attendant and teacher. His father Brendan, who died in 2009, was a British advertising executive and by all accounts also a loving and supportive parent. It was his encouragement that steered Nolan and his younger brother Jonathan towards careers in cinema, taking them to see films like Star Wars and 2001: A Space Odyssey at a formative age, then providing them with a camera to experiment with filmmaking as children.

open image in gallery Christopher Nolan (centre) on the set of 'The Odyssey' ( Universal Studios )

Nolan is himself a father of four children – all young adults now – and it might be tempting, then, to view his work not through the lens of his childhood, but his present-day fatherhood. Watching The Odyssey, you would assume that he relates less to Telemachus than the beleaguered patriarch Odysseus. Both are men in positions of command – Odysseus the Greek military, Nolan a hundreds-strong film crew – with professional duties that pull them away from their family. Both are men at war with time. Yet even this reading risks oversimplifying things: work has not really served to scythe Nolan from his family. Increasingly, it seems like the opposite is true. His wife, Dame Emma Thomas, is a producer who has collaborated with him on every one of his films. His children all worked on The Odyssey behind the scenes; no one was left behind in Ithaca.

There is, however, another major family dynamic in Nolan’s life, and here’s where things get interesting. Nolan is one of three brothers. The younger, Jonathan, is a screenwriter and producer who has worked on several of Nolan’s films. The elder is not. Matthew Nolan, closer in age to Chris and based in America, was arrested by the FBI in 2009, when Costa Rican authorities sought to extradite him on a murder charge. (It was claimed, in one of the court documents, that he was a contract killer.) Matthew denied it, and a US federal judge found the “hitman” claim lacking in evidence, refusing to extradite him; he was nonetheless sentenced to a stint in prison after attempting to escape from jail in Chicago. Neither of his brothers have ever discussed the case publicly.

A 2010 report in The Times notes that Matthew, supposedly the more charismatic of the three brothers, “might have been expected to be the one to become the successful filmmaker”, and that he joined Chris in filmmaking follies as a child. The pair had, it adds, “drifted apart over the years, and now it’s Chris and Jonah who are friends and collaborators, despite their greater age difference”.

open image in gallery Matt Damon and Zendaya in 'The Odyssey' ( Melinda Sue Gordon )

For all Nolan’s silence when it comes to his brother, it’s hard not to speculate how this bizarre – and, one can only assume, impactful – part of his family history has imprinted itself on his work. Is it meaningful that his films have revisited the idea of international criminality? Several of his characters lead double lives; some are on the run from the law. One of the allegations to emerge from the reports around Matthew was that he went by the false name of “Matthew McCall Oppenheimer”, in an attempt to link himself to a powerful diamond family – the connection to Christopher Nolan’s 2023 film Oppenheimer is a coincidence, for sure, but one that inevitably raises eyebrows.

Ultimately, when it comes to these resonances in Nolan’s oeuvre, everything is guesswork – a squint for cohesion as if it were a Magic Eye picture. But there’s no getting around how curious it is for a director who grew up with such noteworthy brothers to be so reluctant to explore sibling dynamics on screen. Maybe the choice is telling.

The conclusion we might reach is that Nolan is just unwilling to make his films personal. These are works of mass entertainment, after all. But, as the great Italian filmmaker Federico Fellini once said, all art is autobiographical. In some ways, The Odyssey, and its predecessor Oppenheimer, have given us the clearest picture of Nolan’s mind to date: these are films charged with political anger, an artist reckoning with the moral weight of war and foreign policy. (Discussions over whether or not Nolan’s films are subtly right-wing, which peaked around the time of Dunkirk, have largely dissipated.)

But while he has started to open up politically, his personal life remains a mystery. Perhaps, one day, he will address it head on, as Spielberg did with The Fabelmans, a confessional late-career masterpiece that served as a cipher key to much of his life’s work. Or he won’t. But film by film, it becomes increasingly clear that Nolan is a major auteur, one whose films cannot be dismissed as mere diversion. For people to scour his movies for personal revelation – to, as he puts it, “have me in mind when they’re watching the films” – is simply to treat his work with the seriousness it deserves. Whether he likes it or not.

‘The Odyssey’ is in UK cinemas now

News.title: Spain win World Cup in triumph of football over Argentine felony
News.content:
Spain should have won far more comfortably but the European champions lived up to the claim made by their coach Luis de la Fuente and proved they are the best team in the world – as they won this tournament for the second time and for the first since 2010 – having beaten the favourites France in the last four. They were worthy winners.

There is another European nation chasing that second star, the one beaten by Argentina in Atlanta last Wednesday.

If England ever want to win this again then here is the blueprint. From Spain. This is how the game should be played. Get the ball, keep the ball, love the ball, move the ball. Try to play. Be brave and stay brave. It is not complicated, but it requires a re-education.

Maybe one day English football will grow up and cherish ball-players of their own rather than Manchester City sign Rodri, who was magnificent here until he tired, or Arsenal Martín Zubimendi, who successfully replaced him.

Rodri was rightly named player of the tournament, in recognition of the football his nation played and the 30-year-old’s importance to that. He is their heartbeat and metronome. England do not just need to find a Rodri but cherish whoever that is.

News.title: Hamilton takes out Russell as Antonelli stretches lead with Belgian GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: Ryan Fox matches father Grant’s sporting folklore with Claret Jug
News.content:
It’s the final day of the Open Championship, golf’s oldest and most-prestigious major. The leaderboard offers up hope of a seesaw day where little-known-of golfers tussle it out with big names under the north-west English sun. All in all, it should be an exciting day.

But, as with the past two days, we head into the round with talk dominated by a certain Bryson DeChambeau. It’s as frustrating and annoying as it is, in these days dominated by social media/content etc etc, painfully predictable. So let’s get the DeChambeau news out the way. Having been fairly hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on Friday, the YouTube content creator had a tantrum, threatened to withdraw, caused a delay in the release of third-round tee times, before turning up and shooting a one-under 69 to lie four behind the leader heading into today.

That’s not all, The Bryson DeChambeau Show carried on after yesterday’s round where James Corrigan takes up the script...

Bryson DeChambeau marched straight to the offices of the R&A after being heckled with a cry of “you’re a cheat” on Birkdale’s 18th green on Saturday. As the controversy over his two-shot penalty from Friday’s second round rumbled on, Telegraph Sport understands DeChambeau, who shot a third-round 69 to lie four shots off the lead of the Open, asked R&A chief executive Mark Darbon for his scorecard from Friday. It is against policy so his request was rejected. DeChambeau then went back to the recorder’s hut and asked if they had it. Again, the answer was in the negative. It is unclear why he wanted it, but a theory emerged that he wished to put it on his social media channels.

All in all it is pathetic posturing that you’d expect from a stroppy teenager. He’s only three off the lead and has the game to win at Royal Birkdale, he’d do well to forget the perceived slights (whatever they may be) and get on with trying to win the Claret Jug.

Oh, and to add another scene to the soap opera Rory McIlroy doubtless spoke for many inside and outside the rope when he called out DeChambeau saying: “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

So, I think it’s best we focus on the golf today and not the theatrics and sorry antics of the American.

Sam Burns, his playing partner yesterday, was brilliant as he backed up his 62 of Friday with a five-under 65. He leads by two on 10 under and is the man to beat. Lurking behind with intent are a host of big names and big hitters – Ryan Fox (eight under), Si Woo Kim (eight under), Lucas Herbert (six under), Ludvig Aberg (seven under) and the man himself YouTube’s very own DeChambeau (six under).

Also in with a hint of a hope is Tommy Fleetwood, the hometown boy in search of his first major, the Englishman will start the round on five under.

Stay here for all the action, where I hope all the talk during and after the day’s round is focused on the winner’s brilliance rather than the emotions of DeChambeau.

News.title: Records tumble at Lord’s as England win thriller against India
News.content:
When he fell, bowled trying to sweep Bethell, India were 260 for two, still a tough ask but not impossible, especially against an England side with plenty of demons. Kohli fired up in Rohit’s absence, hitting Will Jacks for two sixes and Bethell into the pavilion.

But the run-rate faltered as Curran whipped out his slower-ball bag of tricks. He had Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer caught in the deep by sub Rehan Ahmed in the 44th over and Kohli in the next, slapping a catch to cover. The rest subsided, India short in the end at 360 for seven.

England’s ODI side have struggled for runs under Brendon McCullum and this was easily their best batting performance, not just for the collection of records but for the calm, controlled way they went about setting a huge total. The openers Duckett and Bethell gave them a 192-run cushion, Root was impregnable again and Buttler finished it off, proving what he can do when others give him a platform. India were without Jasprit Bumrah but that should not take the shine off England’s achievements.

This was the first Duckett-Bethell opening contribution and it was England’s highest for the first wicket since the last World Cup. Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow were such an important part of the route to World Cup glory and they left a huge hole in the side. Duckett and Bethell are more touch players, capable of gear shifts rather than setting out at turbo pace like Roy and Bairstow. The fact they bat so often together in Test cricket, where Bethell appears at No 3, helps the level of understanding.

Duckett’s innings knocked Viv Richards’s 138 in the 1979 World Cup final off the top spot at Lord’s and continued the form he showed at the end of the New Zealand Test series when he scored his first Test hundred in nearly a year. He was out first ball in the second ODI in Cardiff but was never in any real bother at Lord’s as he compiled a fourth century in this format.

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

Sports.title: World Cup final ratings: Lionel Messi does a disappearing act as Nico Williams steps off the bench to win it for Spain
Sports.content:
SPAIN sealed World Cup glory with an extra-time victory over Argentina – and it was two substitutes who made the difference.

Ferran Torres climbed off the bench to grab a 106th minute winner in the outskirts of New York.



The former Manchester City man reacted quickest following a knock-down from Nico Williams, who had a goal of his own controversially ruled out.

It allowed Spain to win the tournament for the second time – having also got their hands on the sport’s biggest prize in 2010.



And it ended Argentina’s hopes of defending the title they won in Qatar four years ago.

SunSport’s Shaun Custis and Dean Scoggins have given their verdict on the performances in the World Cup final



SPAIN

UNAI SIMON – 6/10

Not his busiest of days but undoubtedly has a composure about him and was always alert to the through ball. A calming influence for his defence.

PEDRO PORRO – 6

He has not always been an assured presence during Spurs’ struggles. However, he has certainly looked the part for Spain in this tournament both in defence and attack.

PAU CUBARSI – 7

What a talent this young defender is. Still only 19 yet he is an established centre-back for Barcelona and Spain. Wonderful passer of a football. Fouled by Enzo Fernandez who was sent off for a second yellow.

AYMERIC LAPORTE – 7

Seems to have found his form again since leaving Manchester City. Has established a good double-act with young Cubarsi and had a header saved by Emiliano Martinez.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

MARC CUCURELLA – 7

There were those who thought he was a bit of a clown when he first signed for Chelsea. Has now joined Real Madrid and easy to see why. Gave Spain defensive quality as well as an attacking option.

RODRI – 7

What more can be said about Man City’s former Ballon d’Or winner? He controlled the midfield and frustrated his opponents, so much so Leandro Parades elbowed him in the back and was deservedly booked.

FABIAN RUIZ – 6

Has grown into one of the most versatile midfielders in football. Having won the Champions League at PSG, this was another big evening in his career but had a quiet game. Subbed off for Pedri.

DANI OLMO – 6

Took a hefty early challenge from Alexis Mac Allister, who seems to turn into rent-a-thug in a blue and white shirt. Olmo tried to be creative but was given a constant kicking.



ALEX BAENA – 5

It’s not easy to impress when your team-mates are usually looking for Lamine Yamal on the other flank and Baena struggled to get into the game here. Replaced by the far more effective Williams.

LAMINE YAMAL – 6

Was perhaps expected to make his mark on this World Cup more than he has. Showed flashes of his genius and had a free-kick well saved by Martinez.

MIKEL OYARZABAL – 5

Considering he is the go-to striker for one of the world’s best international teams he flies under the radar. Had one shot easily saved and took a nasty whack from Lisandro Martinez before being subbed.



SUBSTITUTES:

Ferran Torres for Oyarzabal (62mins) – 6

Spain needed a poacher to break the deadlock and Torres provided.

Pedri for Fabian Ruiz (62mins) – 5

Nico Williams for Baena (75mins) – 7

Was the star man. Attacking threat when he came on. Great nod back for the winner.



Mikel Merino for Olmo (75mins) – 5

Eric Garcia for Laporte (99mins) – 5

Martin Zubimendi for Rodri (99mins) – 5



ARGENTINA

EMILIANO MARTINEZ – 7

Excellent late save from Yamal in normal time before another stunner kept out Williams as he kept Argentina in it. Most of the other Spain shots were straight at him. Fumbled an Olmo shot on the hour and flapped at a corner. Organised his back line well.

GONZALO MONTIEL – 5

Bizarre mix of charging forward to occupy a right-wing position on the rare occasion Argentina had the ball, and charging back to try and get to Cucurella when they lost it. Good battle with Baena though. Subbed before the hour.

CRISTIAN ROMERO – 7

By far Argentina’s best player, on and off the ball. Coped with the Spain runners, made tackles and still found the energy to bark at anyone who came near him. Incredibly, the calm head in the backline this time until being subbed with injury.

LISANDRO MARTINEZ – 3

Very nervous start, almost poked into his own net from a Yamal shot and twice passed the ball out of play under no pressure. Injured himself with a poorly-timed tackle on Ruiz and got subbed. Saved from himself, really.

NICO TAGLIAFICO – 6

Good battle with Yamal, but struggled with his pace, fouling him on the halfway line the main tactic. Lucky to escape giving the ball away twice after the half-time snooze fest but stuck to his task well.



NICOLAS GONZALEZ – 3

Hooked at half-time after having little impact. One half decent dribble on the left but spent most of his time chasing Porro back to his own goal.

ENZO FERNANDEZ – 5

Tireless effort and was run ragged by the Spanish. Little impact going forward, but none of the Argentines did. Was finally booked for backchat on 80 minutes and then was late on Cubarsi for a second yellow.

ALEXIS MAC ALLISTER – 6

Made a real impact… on Olmo’s legs, with two crunching first half tackles that somehow didn’t see a card. Worked incredibly hard to stay with the Spanish runners in midfield and tried, without much joy, to get them going in attack. Finally booked in extra-time.



RODRIGO DE PAUL – 5

Messi’s minder was more like Montiel’s minder in this one, spending half of his time doubling up going back to help his defence, with Cucurella providing plenty of problems. Industrious as ever.

JULIAN ALVAREZ – 4

More anonymous than Lionel Messi, if that was possible, with only eight touches in the first half. Crowded out most of the time in the second. Lots of runs, not many touches. Pressed so hard that most of the time Spain’s defenders just ran past him.

LIONEL MESSI – 4

The little magician did a disappearing act for most of the game as Argentina could not get him the ball. The usual classy touches but most of them to get his team out of their own half.

SUBSTITUTES:

Nicolas Otamendi for Martinez (44 mins) – 5

Absolute bruiser and took on Rodri at set-pieces. Held his line and kept Argentina battling. Stayed strong and clung onto runners, literally. Dived to get Spain’s goal disallowed in extra-time.



Leandro Paredes for Gonzalez (46 mins) – 3

Booked for his first involvement – a barge off the ball on Rodri. Similar to what he did most of the game against England. Another lunge on Porro later before fouling Torres. Was eventually sent off during a mass brawl after the final whistle.

Secured the right-side when he came on and the Baena-Cucurella attacks subsided afterwards.

Replaced Romero on 70 minutes, but played left centre-back. Did a good job against Torres with Argentina’s backs to the wall. Some big, fair tackles.

Nasty foul on Cucurella late on, having replaced De Paul. Did his defensive work against the Spain left-back.

Sports.title: Piers Morgan leads fans furious at Argentina star Leandro Paredes and blasts Argentina as ‘disgrace to football’
Sports.content:
PIERS MORGAN led the stinging criticism of the Argentine “thugs” who lost to Spain in the World Cup final.

Chaos erupted after Spain‘s extra-time victory, with Argentina‘s Leandro Paredes involved in a nasty scuffle.



Paredes completely lost his head as he sprinted over and shoved Eric Garcia to the ground.

As others from both sides charged over, the Argentine midfielder took aim at Gavi, dragging him to the ground and then striking him while he was down.



Referee Slavko Vincic showed Paredes a straight red card despite the game already being over.

And Arsenal and England fan Morgan had seen enough to let rip on social media.

He wrote on X: “Disgusting behaviour by the Argentinians at the end, especially Paredes.

Argentina had made themselves more unpopular among England fans during the two nations’ semi-final on Wednesday.

Valentin Barco and Cristian Romero both celebrated goals in the faces of England players, and Argentina toasted the victory with a banner about the Falklands.

Sports.title: Awkward moment Infantino forced to rescue Trump as he lingers on stage while World Cup winners Spain wait to lift trophy
Sports.content:
DONALD Trump was caught out almost photobombing the victorious Spanish team as he lingered on the stage while they patiently waited to lift the World Cup.

The president couldn’t seem to resist hovering onstage after handing over the trophy as the Spanish side celebrated their win over Argentina, with Fifa boss Gianni Infantino forced to rush back to guide him away.



Trump joined Fifa President Infantino at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey to present the trophy to the winners after their 1-0 victory on Sunday.

The President handed out gold medals to Spain and the referees, as well as silver medals to Argentines.



He was joined onstage by the leaders of his co-host nations – Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum.

But after handing out the trophy with Infantino, Trump didn’t appear to want to get out of Spain’s shot.



Infantino walked off one side of the stage as the Spaniards waited to hoist the cup, but Trump continued to talk to the players before standing to the side of the team.

Some of the Spanish team even looked like they were going to coax Trump into his famous YMCA dance.

The Fifa boss jogged back across the stage as he tried to usher Trump to the side.

He eventually succeeded as the Spanish team began their celebrations to roars from thousands in the crowd.



Trump could be seen again pausing at the side of the stage as he watched gold ticker tape rain down on the winners.

Spain beat defending champions Argentina in their second-ever World Cup win.

Trump watched the game from a box with his fellow world leaders and Infantino while protected by bullet-proof glass.



Football superfan son Barron was also in attendance, and chatted to Infantino and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney before the game.

First lady Melania Trump beamed as the crowd greeted her, wearing a bomber jacket with a red, white, and blue collar.

It came after Trump issued a request to Infantino to allow the World Cup to return to the US “immediately.”

“Based on the numbers we will be requesting it immediately,” he told Fox Sports. We have to do this again, and we have to do this again while I am around, hear that Gianni?”

Under Fifa rules, the US would not be eligible to host until 2038.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi in tears as devastated Argentina players collapse to pitch after agonising World Cup final defeat to Spain
Sports.content:
FOUR days after shedding tears of joy in Atlanta, Argentina players were crying tears of despair in New Jersey.

Their World Cup campaign, and almost certainly Lionel Messi‘s World Cup career, ended with a timid 1-0 defeat to Spain in extra-time.



Three shots – none in the regulation 90 minutes – and none of them on target.

Spain rained down 20 attempts on Emi Martinez’s goal and finally found the breakthrough when Ferran Torres lashed home in the 106th minute.





In their 2-1 semi-final win on Wednesday, Argentina rubbed both of their goals in England players’ faces.

They then posed with a flag which said: “The Faklands are Argentine”, exposing them to possible disciplinary action from Fifa.

So not many Three Lions fans will have been overcome with sympathy watching Messi sob from the final whistle to the trophy lift.

Neither will those who feel the Argentines got more than their fair share of leniency from referees – not least when Nico Williams’ goal in the final was disallowed for a dubious foul in the build-up.



The initial reaction to the defeat from some Argentina players was outright rage.

Leandro Paredes was shown a post-match straight red card for disgracefully striking Gavi in the face.

WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS



Others, including Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni, joined the tussle.

But the rage soon gave way to devastation.

Giuliano Simeone lay face-down on the turf sobbing.

Nahuel Molina lifted up the collar of his shirt to cover most of his face.

Messi shook hands with Lamine Yamal but was also seen wiping tears from his eyes while sat on the MetLife Stadium pitch, and then again as Spain stepped up to collect their reward.



Others joined him, sat there heartbroken as the reality set in.

They had the chance to cap off the greatest footballer of all time’s international career with back-to-back World Cups, but fell short.

And their heads were bowed after an ultra-conservative game plan that painfully backfired.

Sports.title: ‘It is desperation’ – Wayne Rooney SLAMS Lionel Messi for how he tried to get Spain star Marc Cucurella sent off
Sports.content:
WAYNE ROONEY hit out at Lionel Messi for his “desperation” in trying to get Marc Cucurella sent off during Argentina’s World Cup final defeat to Spain.

Argentina’s talisman was involved in a confrontation with new Real Madrid man Cucurella in feisty scenes towards the end of Spain’s 1-0 triumph.



There was a row between both sets of players after Enzo Fernandez was dismissed for sending Pau Cubarsi flying.

Messi was seen having heated words with Cucurella before walking away from the defender and pointing at his rival.



Cucurella appeared to put his hands over his mouth – in violation of Fifa‘s rules – but Rooney wasn’t happy with Messi’s antics, calling the situation “sad”.

The ex-England skipper told BBC Sport: ‘It is desperation. Argentina play like that, we know that’s what they do.

“But the one thing you want is good sportsmanship and that was sad to see Lionel Messi doing that.”

Rooney’s fellow pundits were equally surprised at Messi’s behaviour as Joe Hart claimed the scenes showed how dominant Spain were in the game.

He said: “Oh wow. Wow! Yeah, I didn’t enjoy that at all from Lionel Messi.

“You realise how on top Spain are if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that.”



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

And Micah Richards wasn’t too impressed either as he added: “We don’t want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that.”

There was also stern criticism from Piers Morgan – a known fan of Messi’s rival Cristiano Ronaldo – as he called him a “nasty little sneak”.

It all ended on a low note for Messi as his Argentina side were beaten 1-0 by Spain in extra time after Ferran Torres‘s extra time winner.

The 2022 world champions didn’t even have a shot on target during the entire 120 minutes.



Luis de la Fuente’s men had 65 per cent of the ball and ended up with 20 shots, 12 of which were on target.

Spain easily could have gone 1-0 up earlier on after Nico Williams put the ball in the back of the net – only for the strike to be disallowed due to a foul on Nicolas Otamendi.

There was more frustration from Argentina players after the final whistle as a number of stars were involved in a mass brawl.

Some players were seen pushing and shoving each other as tensions threatened to spill over – with Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni forced to step in and stop it.

Sports.title: FIFA must punish Argentina over three disgraceful World Cup final incidents
Sports.content:
FIFA must punish Argentina over three disgraceful World Cup final incidents

Argentina laid on a clinic in how not to play and how not to behave in their World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes was sent off for violent conduct

Should that be the last we ever see of Lionel Messi at a World Cup - it was a sorry way to bow out.

‌



Argentina's tournament ended in disgrace and despite their captain's genius, he could not totally distance himself from what can only be described as a national embarrassment.

‌



After all, it was the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner who tried to engineer Marc Cucurella's dismissal in a sheer act of desperation

‌



The newly-signed Real Madrid left-back admittedly briefly covered his mouth but the 39-year-old veteran and Enzo Fernandez's unsuccessful attempts to snitch on and intimidate Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic were shameful and smacked of desperation.

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni breaks down in tears during quit hint after World Cup final READ MORE :

What Argentina star said to Rodri in furious on-pitch exchange after World Cup final whistle READ MORE :

The great irony was that not only did Fernandez later get sent off following two yellow cards but Nicolas Otamendi also had the audacity to accuse Rodri and Aymeric Laporte of deliberately trying to influence the officials.

The worst - Leandro Paredes' full-time thuggery - was yet to come - however. Losing your cool is one thing but Paredes lost all sense of self-respect as he jostled, wrestled and attacked Eric Garcia and Gavi.

‌



Special mention to right-back Nahuel Molina for not only playing a key part in Ferran Torres' winner but also punching Rodri.

FIFA are yet to punish Argentina's controversial and offensive 'Islas Malvinas' banner post-England but it's about time they threw the book at Lionel Scaloni's side, who also lost huge respect on the day they vacated their World Cup crown.

Paredes and Molina's behaviour in particular was unsavoury, shocking and utterly unsurprising if you watched him in action against England in Atalanta.

‌



His sole primary purpose on the pitch is to startle the opposition and get under their skin. Little wonder he's earned 84 caps.

View 3 Images EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JULY 19: Leandro Paredes of Argentina (5) gets violent against Gavi of Spain (9) after the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

Even Scaloni's assistant coach Raton Ayala thought it was acceptable to put his fist into the face of Spain's Dani Olmo, this is another separate incident that requires policing.

‌



Rather mysteriously, Valentin Barco was nowhere to be seen. He was happy to shout and celebrate wildly - invading the field from the bench - in the face of Jude Bellingham but when Spain were crowned champions, he was nowhere to be seen.

Fernandez's midweek 'Wonderwall' Instagram post mocking England also backfired spectacularly and blew up in his face.

Argentina then took it upon themselves to turn their backs to Spain as La Roja made their way onto the podium to lift the iconic gold trophy - it was a staggering lack of basic respect.

‌



This is all without considering how badly Argentina actually played. They did not have a single shot until the 116th minute.

View 3 Images Lionel Messi tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off

Spain centre-back Laporte actually referenced that both he and his teammates felt Argentina went overboard in midweek.

‌



The newly-crowned world champions do not do things in half measures and therefore, saw no reason to revel in the glory of Tuesday's semi-final triumph over France.

Scaloni claimed his players were a "great example for our people and country," and ultimately, if they are honestly a true reflection of the nation's population, it's hard to see Argentina ever being universally popular.

It's a miracle the final was so one-sided when you consider the South Americans were also the only team not to have a single VAR intervention against them, they received the most penalties, had the most opposition goals chalked off, the most opposition yellow cards awarded and they also travelled the least out of all the 48 competing nations.

Article continues below

Equally, it would have been the biggest injustice since Folarin Balogun's red card was overturned had Argentina won.

Liverpool round-up as one of the Europe's most exciting young players becomes available

A crucial pre-season is underway at Liverpool as Andoni Iraola attempts to revive the club's fortunes following a torrid title defence. Preparations will move up a notch next weekend when the Reds face Sunderland in Nashville.

‌



Further friendlies in the US, against Wrexham and Leeds United, will follow before home games against Monaco and Como ahead of the Premier League opener at Newcastle on August 23.

‌



Two new players have joined the club so far this summer, with Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz arriving from Rennes and Osasuna, respectively. However, much more remedial work is needed if Liverpool are to launch a title challenge this season.

‌



World Cup stars Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola are among a host of players to be linked with a move to Anfield. As new campaign edges closer, here's a round-up of some of the latest Reds news…

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Reds beat Bayern

Liverpool have beaten Bayern Munich to the signing of Samuel Martinez. As reported by the Liverpool Echo, the Reds have agreed a fee of around £740,000 with Atletico Nacional for the attacking midfielder.

‌



As part of the deal, he will remain at the Colombian side for a further 12 months and will arrive during next summer's transfer window after turning 18 in April. The 17-year-old was wanted by a host of European giants, including Barcelona and Borussia Dortmund.

It has also emerged that Bayern were strong contenders for Martinez's signature. The youngster had been on the radar of the German champions for months and was on their summer target list, reports TZ . Bayern scouts are said to have likened Martinez's style of play to that of Brazilian legend Kaka.

They also had a trump card in the shape of the player's agent, Daniel Neumuller, who is from Bavaria. However, it is Liverpool who appear to have won the race to sign him, even if fans will have to wait a year to see him in the flesh.

‌



Mbaye on the move

The Reds have been put on alert after Ibrahim Mbaye of Paris Saint-Germain was made available for transfer. It's no secret that the Reds are in the market for a wide man or two.

View 2 Images Ibrahim Mbaye looks set to leave PSG (Image: Getty Images)

Hopes of signing Diomande appear to have faded, with the Ivorian reportedly holding out for a move to PSG and prepared to spend another season at RB Leipzig. Therefore, Liverpool may turn to 18-year-old Mbaye, one of the most exciting young talents in Europe.

‌



According to Fabrizio Romano, the Senegal star will leave PSG this summer, with super agent Jorge Mendes said to be "in control of his future." The report adds that Premier League and Bundesliga clubs are on standby to take advantage of the situation.

While competition will be intense, the Reds would be an attractive proposition given the obvious vacancy on the right flank following Mohamed Salah's departure .

Sports.title: Argentina's president Javier Milei declares bank holiday after World Cup loss to Spain
Sports.content:
Argentina's president Javier Milei declares bank holiday after World Cup loss to Spain

Argentina's loss in the final has been greeted with a bank holiday by the country's president, Javier Milei, who said Messi and co will decide when it takes place hours after Spain lifted the trophy

View 4 Images (Image: Getty Images)

Argentina will enjoy a national holiday despite losing the World Cup final, the country's president has announced.

‌



The South Americans lost 1-0 to Spain in New Jersey on Sunday (July 19), defeated by a Ferran Torres strike in extra time. By that point, Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez - who scored to break English hearts in the semi-finals - had been sent off for Argentina.

‌



The spectacle descended into chaos after full time, when clashes broke out between both sets of players. Argentina's Leandro Parades was sent off for kicking out and shoving his opponents to the ground after the final whistle had gone.

‌



Lionel Messi, who likely has played his final World Cup game aged 39, was in tears after the tournament finished. It was his third final and second loss, having beaten France in Qatar four years ago, but losing to Germany 1-0 in extra time at the 2014 tournament hosted in Brazil.

Several hours after Spain lifted the trophy with Donald Trump photobombing proceedings, Argentina's president, Javier Milei, announced the country is in line for a bank holiday. Unlike Spanish dignitaries, Milei did not attend the final, citing superstition.

However, the national holiday date will be chosen by Argentina's players, not the government, he added.

‌



View 4 Images Ugly scenes dominated the aftermath as Argentina and Spain clashed

An English translation of Milei's post in X in Spanish said: " WORLD CELEBRATION.

"Given the concern about the celebrations for the achievement reached by the Argentine National Team, I inform the population that, depending on what the players and the technical staff decide regarding the day to celebrate, it will be declared a national holiday."

‌



Argentinians enjoyed a bank holiday after winning the 2022 World Cup. It occurred on the Tuesday after the final, when players returned to Buenos Aires for a parade.

Four years ago, it seemed like Argentina had the football world at its feet. However, it now appears the team will undergo a period of rebuilding.

View 4 Images Rodri lifted the World Cup for Spain

‌



Head coach Lionel Scaloni left his press conference in tears after the final, when he was asked if he would take the team forward after his contract expires in December.

“I have to be honest and say that I have to take time and think about the future,” the victorious Qatar 2022 coach said. “Because I’m not sure this can be achieved again.”

Argentina will almost certainly go into the next World Cup without star skipper Messi, who sobbed after what looks to be his last game on the global stage. Messi is 39 years old and would be 43 by the time the next World Cup comes around, held in Spain, Portugal, and Morocco - with three matches played in South America to mark the tournament's 100th birthday.

‌



“He is 39 years old, it is unbelievable,” Scaloni said. “It was always crystal clear to me that he would play until he chose to stop and that everyone would support him.

“I hope everyone is proud of him, because he is the best football player ever to set foot on a pitch.”

View 4 Images Lionel Scaloni faces a tricky rebuild

‌



Captain Messi is 39 years old and would be 43 by the time the next World Cup comes around, held in Spain, Portugal, and Morocco - with three matches played in South America to mark the tournament's 100th birthday.

However, Scaloni was magnanimous in defeat, attempting to stop his players from fighting Spaniards at full time. He also accepted Spain were the better team.

He went on: “I feel sadness but knowing that we left everything out there. I have a lot of things to say about how we got here, but it’s not worth it.

Article continues below

“I want to thank these guys eternally for giving us another World Cup final and for competing until the end. They were better, that’s the truth.

“But I’ll hold on to an enormous memory of what they have done, of what it’s worth to get this far. We have to give it huge validity because it takes a lot to get here.”

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Morgan Rogers' three reasons for snub as Gunners enquire about £110m hijack
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Morgan Rogers' three reasons for snub as Gunners enquire about £110m hijack

A look at the latest transfer headlines surrounding Arsenal

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers has snubbed Arsenal for Chelsea (Image: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal are set to move on from their pursuit of Morgan Rogers after Chelsea hijacked their pursuit. The Gunners had been linked with the Aston Villa attacker for some time but the Blues have shocked their city rivals by jumping in on the signing.

‌



Rogers will sign a six-year deal at Stamford Bridge and become a club-record acquisition for a fee of £117million. Mikel Arteta will move on from this transfer failure and keep pushing for more signings.

‌



Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier have already signed permanent deals with Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola and Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi both linked. The Gunners have also been connected with a surprise move for a £110m star who turned down Liverpool.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of the Emirates Stadium.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rogers' reasoning for Arsenal snub

Rogers was given three simple reasons to join Chelsea over Arsenal, despite being heavily linked with the Gunners. The Athletic reported that the midfielder opted for the Blues due to the exciting project that had been sold to him by the club.

‌



As well as this, Xabi Alonso's presence at Stamford Bridge was another way that Chelsea convinced him to snub Arsenal. It's also understood that the Blues have informed Rogers that they intend to utilise him out on the left wing next season, which ended up being the cherry on top of his impending move.

View 3 Images Rogers was given three reasons to join the Blues (Image: Aston Villa/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

The 23-year-old is expected to undergo a medical to become a Chelsea player this week, with the club paying Aston Villa £117m for his services. This means that Rogers has surpassed the Blues' record signing fee, which was previously Enzo Fernandez's £107m arrival in 2023.

‌



Gunners eye £110m hijack

Arsenal are moving on from their failed pursuit of Rogers and could instead hijack Paris Saint-Germain's move for Yan Diomande. The RB Leipzig winger had been heavily linked with Liverpool earlier in the transfer window, with the Reds submitting a £86.8m bid.

View 3 Images Yan Diomande is being linked with various clubs this summer (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

However, it was said that Diomande was keen on moving to France instead, with Leipzig valuing him at a whopping £110m (€130m). The 19-year-old has agreed personal terms with PSG with L'Equipe reporting that a fee is being negotiated.

Article continues below

According to Fabrizio Romano, though, the Gunners enquired with his agents in recent days to see if there was a chance of signing him. The Gunners would have to fork out a hefty amount to secure the teenager but may be planning a more forceful approach after losing out on Rogers to Chelsea.

Sports.title: Tottenham star Cristian Romero 'snubs' Trump handshake after World Cup final
Sports.content:
Tottenham star Cristian Romero 'snubs' Trump handshake after World Cup final

The Tottenham Hotspurs player was caught on camera seemingly blanking the 47th American president's offered handshake during a presentation of runners-up medals in the minutes after the last whistle at the 2026 World Cup final

View 2 Images Cristian Romero went off injured in the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

Tottenham star Cristian Romero appeared to snub US President Donald Trump's handshake during a presentation of runners-up medals at the 2026 World Cup final.

‌



Spain won the World Cup after beating the defending champions 1-0 in extra time, with Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal after Argentina were reduced to 10 men when Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the 93rd minute.

‌



But despite being subbed off by Argentina, 28-year-old defender Romero still managed to make his mark on the match by appearing to ignore Trump.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

In now-viral footage circulating on social media, Romero can be seen shaking the hand of both Fifa president Gianni Infantino and Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum, who were either side of Trump. The Spurs star can also be seen glazing over the US president in the middle, as Trump helped by handing out medals to both teams. The awkward Trump moment was the third in a hat trick of awkward moments for the US President. Shortly before kick-off, Trump appeared on the giant screens inside MetLife Stadium. The cheers that had accompanied the national anthem just moments before quickly gave way to a chorus of boos, whistles, and jeers directed at the president, who had arrived via the Marine One helicopter and made a dramatic flyover of MetLife Stadium before the match got under way. Trump had been keen to avoid a repeat of his viral New York Knicks moment, while security teams left absolutely nothing to chance. F-16 fighter jets, military marksmen, and thousands of FBI agents were deployed to safeguard MetLife Stadium and the surrounding airspace.

‌



View 2 Images Donald Trump gatecrashes Spain's World Cup trophy lift (Image: Getty Images)

The match has been designated a "Level 1" special event - the highest security classification in the US - putting it on par with presidential inaugurations and State of the Union addresses. It didn't get much better after the match for Trump, with celebrating Spainiards briefly siding with the Argentinians in the crowd once again as it seemed the entire stadium became a cacophony of boos and jeers shortly after the last whistle of the 2026 World Cup. Footage shared on social media showed crowds heckling the 47th President of the United States as he walked across the grass to the centre of the pitch in order to present Spain with the World Cup trophy.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Article continues below

Seemingly unbothered by the hissing crowd, Trump then refused to leave the podium after presenting Spain with the World Cup trophy, making his presence at the World Cup even more awkward. After the final whistle, the Spanish players walked onto the podium individually to collect their medals before US President Trump and Gianni Infantino presented them with the World Cup trophy. But instead of stepping aside once the presentation was over, Trump stayed on stage, shaking hands with players and raising his fists in the air as the celebrations got underway. Infantino appeared to try to usher a seemingly uncertain Trump away from the team, but the US President remained standing to the right of the squad as they celebrated, overshadowing what was meant to be Spain's trophy-lift moment.

Sports.title: Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni breaks down in tears during quit hint after World Cup final
Sports.content:
Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni breaks down in tears during quit hint after World Cup final

Lionel Scaloni's Argentina contract expires in December and he's indicated he could yet depart his role after failing to guide his team a second consecutive World Cup

View 2 Images Lionel Scaloni was deeply emotional after Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain

Lionel Scaloni has hinted he could quit his role as Argentina head coach upon the expiry of his contract later this year.

‌



The 48-year-old, who has guided La Albiceleste to two Copa Americas, one World Cup and La Finalissima since taking up the role in 2018, has a deal which runs until December.

‌



While Scaloni will speak to the Argentinian Football Association regarding fresh terms, he insists there is a chance he could call time on his illustrious spell at the helm.

‌



He said during an emotional post-match press conference: "I haven't spoken with Leo [Messi]. As for me, I'm going to talk to the president. I have an idea of what I want to do.

What Argentina star said to Rodri in furious on-pitch exchange after World Cup final whistle READ MORE :

Donald Trump crashes Spain's World Cup trophy moment and humiliates FIFA boss READ MORE :

"I'll fulfil the contract and then we'll see. The truth is, I feel the need to think, because I don't know if I'll be able to do something as big as this.

"Maybe we'll have to talk. I'm grateful to the president for giving me an opportunity like this, for being in this position," before he broke down in tears.

‌



He then continued: "Being in the place I am, a dream come true for everyone. We tried until the very last moment to give our all as a coaching staff and as players. It's only right that I can take this time to think about it. This place is wonderful, a dream come true that I never imagined in my life."

View 2 Images Lionel Scaloni's Argentina contract runs until December

Scaloni then added before abruptly leaving the press conference room: "In my life I never thought, we all thought on the coaching staff, that we'd be in this position.

‌



"So, to continue, a lot of things are needed, especially to reset, to rebuild a group like this, which is unlikely to be formed again, and it pains me deeply."

Argentina were totally outplayed in the World Cup final and had just two shots to Spain's 20.

La Roja had to be patient to eventually break down the door, however, much to the brilliance and resilience of Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez.

Article continues below

Ferran Torres eventually struck the winner after coming off the bench, inflicting the killer blow in the 106th minute after Enzo Fernandez was sent off following two yellow cards.

Sports.title: Spain beat Argentina to win World Cup
Sports.content:
Spain won their second World Cup title after Ferran Torres' 106th-minute smashed finish earned a 1-0 win against defending champions Argentina in the 2026 final.

Spain were deserved winners. Torres scored with Spain's 20th shot while the game ended without Argentina registering a single shot on target.

Lionel Messi touched the ball just 54 times in a match that took three hours to complete and featured a 27-minute half-time break.

Spain's win had shades of their maiden victory in 2010 too, scoring in the second period of extra time after a goalless 90 minutes. Then, it was Andres Iniesta against the Netherlands - now another Barcelona player, Torres, adds his name to the history books.

Image: Spain's Rodri lifts the World Cup

A nod back from fellow substitute Nico Williams saw the former Manchester City forward storm on to the ball and fire past Aston Villa goalkeeper Emi Martinez. It came minutes after Williams had an initial strike ruled out for an alleged Mikel Merino foul on Nicolas Otamendi.

Argentina did keep their shape well as Spain applied consistent pressure - especially after Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez was sent off for a reckless second yellow at the end of normal time - and relied on Martinez to make a string of saves.

Image: Enzo Fernandez fouls Pau Cubarsi resulting in a red card for the Argentina midfielder

Image: Enzo Fernandez was sent off late in the second half as Argentina finished the game with ten players

Their only threat emerged in added-on time at the end of extra time, with Giuliano Simeone blazing over a shot that could have sent the game to penalties.

But there was no fairytale end to Messi's expected final World Cup appearance, with the Argentina skipper anonymous for much of the game. He was also beaten to his first World Cup Golden Boot by France's Kylian Mbappe, who won it by two goals.

Image: A tearful Lionel Messi reacts to Argentina's defeat in the World Cup final (AP Photo/Pamela Smith)

Spain remain undefeated under manager Luis de la Fuente in tournament matches and add a World Cup win to their Euros title from 2024. It has been quite the tournament from an opening draw to Cape Verde to making France and Argentina look like average teams and lifting the World Cup.

Paredes and Molina involved in angry scenes after full-time

Image: Leandro Parades was sent off after the game after starting a brawl with some of Spain's players

There were unsavoury scenes at full-time as Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina looked to strike out at the celebrating Spain players after Argentina's defeat.

Molina threw out an elbow and caught Rodri, while Paredes appeared to kick Eric Garcia to the floor and pushed him back with a strong hand around his neck when the Spaniard got back to his feet to confront him.

A Spain substitute was then held back by another Argentina player before Paredes came in, ripped his bib and swung for him twice, catching him in the face.

Paredes, who came on at half-time, was booked within minutes of coming on and escaped a number of other yellow card offenses. He was eventually sent off in the aftermath of the post-match hostilities.

Image: Spain's Ferran Torres celebrates scoring their winner (AP Photo/Julio Cortez)

5: SHOT! Lamine Yamal has the first shot on target.

39: SHOT! Oyarzabal strikes - but it goes straight at Emi Martinez.

77: CHANCE! Pedro and Pau Cubarsi draw saves from the Argentina goalkeeper as Spain keep pushing for a goal.

90+3: RED CARD! Fernandez sent off for second yellow card after reckless challenge on Cubarsi.

90+9: SAVE! Lamine Yamal forces a great save from Emi Martinez after a whipped effort.

96: NO GOAL! Williams has the ball in the net, but it is ruled out as Merino inadvertently catches Otamendi on the foot in the build-up.

106: GOAL! Torres fires home from Williams' cushioned effort.

114: OFFSIDE! Torres has the ball in the net again, but he is flagged offside.

120+2: OVER! Simeone has the chance to equalise, but sends an effort over the face of goal as Spain win the World Cup.

Image: Spain's Nico Williams reacts after seeing his strike on goal ruled out by VAR

Analysis: Spain worthy World Cup winners

Sky Sports' Adam Bate: "Spain began this World Cup with a goalless draw against Cape Verde but they end it as worthy winners. They beat the favourites in the semi-final and the reigning champions tonight.

"One goal conceded in eight games, never behind in the tournament, they played all the football here. Passed Argentina off the park. The European champions are World Cup winners too. Thoroughly deserved."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferran Torres scores a crucial goal in added time for Spain to make it 1-0 in the World Cup final game against Argentina.

Sky Sports' Gary Neville speaking on ITV: "Spain are not the best individual players, what they are is the best team, the best collective. And also the best system of play.

"I spent a very short time in Spain and what I found was that they were a different technical and tactical level to Premier League teams, their understanding of the game.

"That comes out most in international football when you are playing every four days in 35-degree heat. Technically and tactically, they are outstanding."

Three Spain players win World Cup awards Player of the tournament: Rodri

Golden Glove: Unai Simon

Young player: Pau Cubarsi

Image: Spain's Rodri poses with the award for the tournament's best player (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Image: Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon poses with the Golden Glove award (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Torres: Destiny was written for us to win

Spain forward Ferran Torres to FIFA: "I think in the end the goal came from 47 million people (approximately the population of Spain), not just those of us that are here.

"Today destiny was written, it was made for us to win. We're far from our people today, but we tried to be as close as possible to them.

Image: Ferran Torres celebrates his goal in extra time to win the World Cup for Spain

"Finals are hard. When you have [Lionel] Messi on the opposing team, you do get worried, but we always backed ourselves and tried to show our football and I think we managed to do it once again.

"[It was] a huge relief [to score]. I've been criticised throughout the whole tournament but, as I said before, destiny was written.

"Thanks to God, he always gives me the strength to continue and in the end he grants things to those that most deserve them."

Merino: We knew we were a better footballing side than Argentina

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spanish fans go wild as they claim their second World Cup trophy over Argentina.

Spain's Mikel Merino speaking to ITV: "Unbelievable. It's the perfect moment for us.

"We are such a golden generation with these young players that give everything they have for this country, for these fans. Luckily, we got the trophy today.

"It was a game about concentration. We knew we were a better team in terms of football.

"The pitch was dry, it was a difficult game because they are a very, very competitive side and they know how to make the game difficult for you. I think the team was outstanding today and we deserve it.

"When you are facing a low block and you have a team that is defending in your own box, you have to attack the box with bodies on the line and then control the transitions.

"We have very good players that can cross the ball, big threats in the box and the old-school way of scoring goals and we did it."

Analysis: Messi conspicuous by his absence

Image: Argentina's Lionel Messi missed out on winning his first World Cup Golden Boot

Sky Sports' Charlotte Marsh: "The World Cup game perhaps epitomises the importance of Messi to Argentina in his anonymity.

"They have relied on the 39-year-old time and again in this tournament, and much like a few of his contemporaries, he did go missing in one of the biggest moments.

"However, that wasn't entirely his fault. Argentina had 34.9 per cent possession and were not able to work anything for their star man to use.

"In the final five minutes, Messi had a few glimpses but this time, he and Argentina ran out of time, with no shots registered on target.

"But by his absence and his team unable to provide for him, it shows even more just how much they rely on him for their goals."

Sports.title: 'My hands were all over the place!' - Fox savours dramatic Open win
Sports.content:
Ryan Fox admitted it was a "dream come true" as he defied the nerves to clinch a dramatic victory in The Open at Royal Birkdale.

The 39-year-old New Zealander produced a superb finish to the final round to overtake clubhouse leader Cameron Young and snatch a one-shot win.

Fox, who had carded a 62 on Saturday to put himself in contention to claim a maiden major success, looked to be slipping out of it after making his second bogey of the day at the 11th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the final round of the 154th Open as Fox claimed the victory

Back-to-back birdies at the 13th and 14th put him back in the hunt and he then did well to escape with only a bogey at the 15th after a nightmare lie in a greenside bunker.

He hit back by birdieing the 16th following a brilliant approach and then, after missing a chance at the 17th, nailed two superb shots down the 18th before boldly draining a 12-foot putt to claim the Claret Jug.

"To play that last hole how I did, I stood on the tee and said to my caddie Dean (Smith), we're going to try to win this," said Fox.

"I hit two perfect shots. I'm not sure how I hit the putt. My hands were all over the place. I was just trying to get it towards the hole somewhere. It's surreal that it went in.

"My focus with the putter all day was just take a really deep breath before I hit it and just try to hit a line, and I did that.

Image: Fox celebrates after holing the winning putt

"I don't know how I managed to keep the putter face square enough for that to go on line, but I'll take it.

"Champion Golfer of the Year has got a pretty good ring to it. It is a dream come true.

"You do dream of this moment. I don't know whether I ever thought it was going to become a reality. Now it is, and to have my name etched in the history of the game is pretty awesome. I think it's pretty awesome for New Zealand as well. It's going to be big down there."

Fox is the son of former All Blacks fly-half Grant Fox and the grandson of former New Zealand Test captain Merv Wallace.

"We've got a great history in our family," he said. "I was lucky enough to carve my own path there. I don't know if this tops their achievements, but it's certainly right up there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fox equalled the lowest round in Open history with a third-round 62 at Royal Birkdale

"I spoke to my kids last night, and they said bring back a trophy. I think this is a pretty cool one to bring back for them.

"I don't know if my dad would be able to contain himself when I was coming down the stretch. He's never been one who has been very good if he doesn't have control over things.

"I think when he was playing and in control of the output, under pressure he was fine. But when he doesn't have control, I think he's a nervous wreck. I'm sure he was."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How Fox clinched victory in The Open at Royal Birkdale

'He stayed aggressive'

Sky Sports Golf duo Dame Laura Davies and Andrew Coltart were both full of praise for Fox and the aggressive approach he adopted on the back nine.

Davies said: "He was the most impressive player all day. He stayed aggressive; I don't think he was scared of losing it. If he lost it because he hit a shot that just didn't work out he was prepared to stay aggressive and I firmly believe that's why he did it.

"He hit irons when he had to, but when there was a chance, a sniff of a birdie, the driver was out, full commitment.

"And the way he played 18 I don't think you could have drawn that up any better. Two of the best shots he will ever hit in his life just to hit that green to give himself a chance."

Image: Fox proudly holds the Claret Jug

Coltart added: "I've never seen somebody push through the tape as hard as that right at the end of the tournament to win a major championship.

"At a place like this, too. It was just superb. The 62 on Saturday I think, helped cement his belief in his ability out there.

"While they all struggled with the pressure, he stood tall."

What's next?

The next PGA Tour event is the 3M Open at TPC Twin Cities in Minnesota, beginning Thursday, with early coverage on Sky Sports+ before switching to Sky Sports Golf at 7pm.

The 3M Open is part of a triple-header of live golf on Sky Sports, with the ISPS Handa Senior Open and ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open also live. The women's major season then concludes with the AIG Women's Open from July 30-August 2, also live on Sky Sports Golf. Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract.

Sports.title: 'My heart really sank' - Hamilton relieved mechanic unhurt after hit
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says his "heart really sank" when his Ferrari hit a mechanic in a pit-stop incident that led to the team being fined heavily by Belgian Grand Prix stewards.

Hamilton's right-front tyre struck the mechanic - who was unhurt - after the driver was given the green signal to leave the team's pit box, briefly knocking the crew member, who was in front of the wheel in an attempt to make a front-wing adjustment, to his knees.

Hamilton promptly stopped his car as the mechanic was helped to his feet, before leaving the pit box.

The incident was placed under a post-race stewards' investigation with Ferrari later handed a €30,000 fine, €10,000 of which is suspended for a year.

Ferrari admitted to an "inappropriately late instruction for the wing adjustment, a lack of clear communication and the mechanic's failure to notice the green light" amid a "complex and unusual combination of circumstances" at a stop which Hamilton had first served a five-second penalty before work on the car commenced.

With no fault attributed to the driver, who stewards said had also suffered a "sporting disadvantage" anyway due to the fact he was delayed in leaving the pit stop, Hamilton retained his fourth-place finish in the race.

The result moved Hamilton back into second place ahead of George Russell in the Drivers' Championship with a deficit of 45 points to Kimi Antonelli, the race winner at Spa-Francorchamps.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix

Speaking about the pit stop confusion after the race, Hamilton said his mind had immediately flashed back to an incident at the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix when a botched Ferrari stop for Kimi Raikkonen caused a mechanic, Francesco Cigarini, to suffer a double leg fracture.

Hamilton was therefore relieved to be told that the mechanic involved on Sunday was not injured, when he enquired about him over team radio.

"The green light went and so I went," said Hamilton to Sky Sports F1.

"You're looking over here [to the left at the lights] you're not looking over there so that's more probably on the team, ultimately.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Despite being given a five-second penalty for an opening lap collision with George Russell, Lewis Hamilton was left more frustrated with his performance over the weekend as he finished fourth in Belgium

"But when it happened, then I noticed him and I stopped and it just went through my mind in that moment was back when Kimi hit and [a mechanic] broke a leg and my heart really sank for a second.

"I'm really grateful he's OK."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton crashes at Turn 13 during the final practice session at the Belgian GP

'We could have been challenging for the win' - Hamilton rues consequence of his Saturday crash

Hamilton's stop had already been elongated by the fact that Ferrari's crew had first had to wait five seconds before starting the car's tyre change owing to the serving of a time penalty for causing a collision with Russell at Les Combes on the opening lap.

The clash spun Russell out of the race, although the Mercedes driver later blamed his own car's straight-line speed issues, rather than former team-mate Hamilton, for the incident at the end of the long Kemmel Straight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton

Hamilton also preferred not to focus on the specifics of the collision in his post-race interview, instead taking the blame for not qualifying higher than sixth, which became fifth on the grid due to Lando Norris' engine penalty, after crashing in Saturday's final practice session.

"I don't count on myself [being] unlucky, I think about my mistake that I made yesterday, so I take full responsibility really for the fourth place that I ended up getting," he said.

"I damaged the car then when they rebuilt the car they missed something on the suspension so the balance was completely different so it meant I was probably a good couple of tenths - maybe three tenths - slower than I should have been in qualifying.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow

"Then I ended up further back, got in the incident. Five second penalty, so like a domino effect from a mistake from myself.

"But the team have been doing a great job with strategy, pit stops. We are continuing to improve the car. I think our pace today, without the damage, we could have been challenging for the win."
