Record-breaking Spain

With another clean sheet, the exceptional Spain conceded just once in the entire tournament, setting a new record for fewest goals shipped at any World Cup in history - and this one had more games than any other.

Meanwhile, there will be no second fairytale for the 39-year-old Lionel Messi, who is expected to call time on his international career before the 2030 World Cup.

England fans, meanwhile, may take some solace in a red card costing Argentina after a feisty semi-final defeat.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi criticised for desperate attempt to exploit new World Cup rule immediately after Enzo Fernandez red
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi criticised for desperate attempt to exploit new World Cup rule immediately after Enzo Fernandez red

Lionel Messi showed his desperation by trying to get Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his mouth during the World Cup final.

The Argentina captain hoped to even the scores against Spain seconds after Enzo Fernandez had rightfully been shown a red card.

3 Messi did what he could to flag Cucurella covering his mouth to the officials

Chelsea star Fernandez was sent off in stoppage time of normal time of their 1-0 defeat against Spain after receiving two yellow cards.

Having already been booked for dissent, the 25-year-old was given his marching orders for lunging into a late challenge on Pau Cubarsi.

But in the immediate aftermath of Fernandez’s red card, Argentinian players swarmed around the Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic.

Cucurella was caught on camera speaking with Messi - only for the 39-year-old to report the new Real Madrid star for covering his mouth.

Commentator Jim Proudfoot said on talkSPORT: "Lionel Messi, when he was speaking to the referee, was not happy Marc Cucurella had gone over to one of the Argentinian players with his mouth covered.

"Messi was saying, by the letter of the law now, that should be deemed to be in a confrontational manner, and that should be a red card offence as well. But nothing happened in the aftermath of that."

England legend Wayne Rooney was among the pundits unhappy with Messi's show of bad sportsmanship.

The Manchester United icon said it was 'sad to see' on television coverage and agreed it was a sign of desperation.

"It is (desperation). But Argentina play like that, we know that’s what they do, and the one thing you want is good sportsmanship.

"That was sad to see Lionel Messi doing that."

3 Messi's actions were rightfully criticised by UK pundits Credit: AFP

Messi slammed for trying to get Cucurella sent off

Joe Hart added: "I didn’t enjoy that at all from Lionel Messi.

"Seeing that, you realise how on top Spain are with even Lionel Messi reverting to that."

Lee Dixon, meanwhile, even labelled Messi a 'baby' for his actions during his own tirade on ITV.

“The game has gone if you're getting bookings and red cards for that, to get somebody sent off,” He said live on air.

“You shouldn’t be such a baby to try and get someone sent off for that; it’s ridiculous.”

3 Messi's attempts fell flat as Spain made their extra man advantage count in extra-time Credit: Getty

Earlier in the tournament, Miguel Almiron became the first player to be sent off for covering his mouth after a dispute with a rival player.

Ecuador defender Piero Hincapie was then given a red card in his nation's 2-0 defeat to Mexico in the Round of 32 for the same action.

However, England superstar Jude Bellingham avoided a similar fate when he covered his mouth to speak to Ghana's Jordan Ayew in June.

The rule was introduced by FIFA ahead of the 2026 World Cup as a result of Benfica winger Gianluca Prestianni, who was handed a six-game ban by UEFA for homophobic conduct during a Champions League knockout match with Real Madrid in February.

Sports.title: How long was half-time at World Cup final? FIFA backtrack on promise to Argentina and Spain
Sports.content:
How long was half-time at World Cup final? FIFA backtrack on promise to Argentina and Spain

FIFA backtracked on their promise to Spain and Argentina that the World Cup final half-time show would last only 17 minutes.

With the 2026 World Cup having taken place across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, there were huge plans for the final showpiece at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.



3 Halftime of the World Cup final took 27 minutes Credit: Getty

FIFA ultimately decided to include a half-time show, unprecedented for football, but very much in line with that of the Super Bowl in the NFL.

Madonna, Shakira, Justin Bieber and K-pop boyband BTS co-headlined the show that was orchestrated by Coldplay frontman Chris Martin.

Even The Muppets' main stars Kermit the Frog and Miss Piggy played a role in a show which did not go down well with everyone.



But the event surpassed the 17-minute runtime that was promised by FIFA.

How long was half-time at World Cup final?

From the second the referee blew his whistle to signal the end of the first half to his whistle to begin the second half, the total time elapsed was 27 minutes and 24 seconds.



This is just another delay that has occurred at the final, with the closing ceremony in the build-up to the game between the reigning European champions and the reigning Copa America champions beginning later than scheduled.

This ultimately caused delays to kick-off until six minutes after the scheduled start time.



England icon Stuart Pearce had a withering reaction to what was on show alongside Adrian Durham on talkSPORT's coverage of the final.

During Shakira's performance, Durham explained: "Shakira, it's her fourth World Cup.

3 The star-studded show caused a delay to the start of the second half

"I was there for the first in 2006, she was sensational. She's sensational again. Stuart Pearce, are you into this?"



In response, England legend Pearce said: "Is it really? That's beautiful. She's certainly entertaining the crowd here."

When put to him that his stance may have been 'harsh' on the Colombian singer, he added: "I haven't said anything harsh at all!

"I said it's sensational, she's entertaining the crowd. You've read into that, that I'm a gnarly old fox."

Durham replied: "Your face does not say those words. They might have come out of your mouth, but your face is saying something completely different."



He continued: "Are you suggesting a mixed message? I didn't actually know who it was, to be fair."

3 Wayne Rooney had a hilarious assessment of the World Cup final half-time show Credit: Getty

Pearce then revealed that he thought K-Pop sensations BTS were 'BLT', but Wayne Rooney went even further live on the BBC.

"I like a lot of them artists," he said. "But I thought it was c***."

Aptly, the two sides couldn't be separated after 90 minutes, with Spain edging a 1-0 win after Ferran Torres' goal in extra-time.



Argentina then disgraced themselves at full-time as players were seen throwing punches in ugly post-match scenes.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney gives ruthlessly honest World Cup final half-time show reaction as Stuart Pearce left baffled
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney was left unimpressed by the World Cup final's half-time.

The first-of-its-kind performance saw a host of stars take to the field during the interval at the MetLife Stadium.

3 Justin Bieber was one of four artists to perform during the World Cup final's half-time show Credit: Getty



A show which lasted over 18 minutes was held following the first half between Spain and Argentina.

Madonna, BTS, Justin Bieber and Shakira all performed on the pitch.

Meanwhile, there were cameos from the Muppets as well as World Cup winners Ronaldinho and Ronaldo.

As a result of the half-time show, the break between halves lasted 27 minutes and 24 seconds.

The performances received a rapturous reception inside the stadium.

However, Rooney was not convinced by what he had seen once the BBC coverage returned to the studio.



Asked for his favourite moment from the half-time show by Gabby Logan, the former England captain admitted: "I'll be honest, when it finished.

"I like a lot of them artists, but I thought it was c***."

His blunt assessment stunned Logan as well as fellow pundits Micah Richards and Joe Hart.



talkSPORT verdict

Rooney was not the only onlooker to be left perplexed by the half-time show.

3 Rooney labelled the performances 'c***' in a brutal assessment live on air



talkSPORT's Stuart Pearce had a similar reaction alongside Adrian Durham on our live coverage of the final.

During Shakira's performance, Durham explained: "Shakira, it's her fourth World Cup.

"I was there for the first in 2006, she was sensational. She's sensational again. Stuart Pearce, are you into this?"

In response, England legend Pearce said: "Is it really? That's beautiful. She's certainly entertaining the crowd here."



When put to him that his stance may have been 'harsh' on the Colombian singer, he added: "I haven't said anything harsh at all! I said it's sensational, she's entertaining the crowd. You've read into that, that I'm a gnarly old fox."

Durham replied: "Your face does not say those words. They might have come out of your mouth, but your face is saying something completely different."

3 Pearce admitted he 'did not know who it was' after watching Shakira's performance Credit: Getty

It soon became clear that Pearce did not know who he had been watching perform, though.



He continued: "Are you suggesting a mixed message? I didn't actually know who it was, to be fair."

Pearce then revealed that he thought K-Pop sensations BTS were 'BLT'.

The half-time show followed a two-part closing ceremony prior to the match.

Performances from Robbie Williams and Nicole Scherzinger minutes before kick-off were followed by a speech from actor Tom Cruise.

As a result, the players were late leaving the tunnel to walk out onto the pitch for the national anthems.



This caused kick-off to be delayed by a total of six minutes in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

Sports.title: Is Donald Trump allowed to touch the World Cup trophy? Strict rules come into spotlight at final
Sports.content:
Is Donald Trump allowed to touch the World Cup trophy? Strict rules come into spotlight at final

Donald Trump has taken a hands-on approach to the World Cup final after being spotted touching the trophy before the end of the game.

The 80-year-old has become the first sitting US president to attend a World Cup final on home soil after heading to MetLife Stadium.

3 Donald Trump has played a hands-on role at the 2026 World Cup Credit: AFP

At the 1994 World Cup, the Jules Rimet trophy wasn't presented by Trump's predecessor Bill Clinton, with his vice president, Al Gore, instead assuming the responsibility of handing it to Dunga.

However, as first revealed by talkSPORT in June, Trump has been given a licence to join the World Cup winners in their trophy lift.

The 45th and 47th US President caused a stir when he accompanied Chelsea on stage for their Club World Cup triumph last summer.

And fans were similarly unhappy to see Trump get his hands on FIFA's illustrious prize in the early stages of Spain against Argentina.

The American billionaire was captured by TV cameras sitting alongside his wife Melania and FIFA chief Gianni Infantino.

The latter then gave the president the go-ahead to touch the World Cup trophy when it was presented to him by Brazilian legend Ronaldo.

Is Trump allowed to touch the World Cup trophy?

Yes, Trump is part of a select group permitted by FIFA to put their hands on football's greatest prize.

FIFA permit heads of state and previous tournament winners to touch the trophy, with Trump qualifying under the former category.

The Republican Party leader was previously granted this honour when FIFA president Infantino visited the White House last year.

3 Trump was FIFA president Gianni Infantino's guest of honour at the final Credit: Getty

3 He was spotted grabbing the World Cup trophy shortly after kick-off Credit: BBC

If Trump gets his way, then it won't be the last time he gets the chance to present the World Cup trophy in his lifetime.

In an interview with Fox’s Jenny Taft ahead of the final, he said: “Well, I had an idea for Gianni. So he got it all started and, you know, I brilliantly said, ‘Well, we’ll do it,’ but, you know, you could have a lot of empty stadiums. (It) didn’t work out that way.

“I think I saw 99.9 per cent, and it’s probably wrong because I think they were overflowing, actually. But I had a great idea for Gianni. I said, ‘You have to do two countries.’ So announce us again next time, and announce another country after that; that’ll take out some of the anger and the shock.”

“I think it’s a great idea,” he continued. “But based on the numbers, we will be requesting it again immediately. But I said to take out the shock, you could announce us and maybe then for the next one another, and even another.

“But we have to do this again, and we have to do it while I’m around. You hear that, Gianni?”

Unfortunately for Trump, the next unassigned World Cup is not until 2038 when he would be 92-years old.

Sports.title: Spain fans target Gianni Infantino as Argentina ‘bias’ conspiracies dominate World Cup final
Sports.content:
Spain fans directed chants towards FIFA president Gianni Infantino just minutes into the World Cup final amid questionable decisions.

Referee Slavko Vincic is the first-ever Slovenian to take charge of football's biggest match.



4 Vincic was on the end of furious chants from Spain fans after a contentious early decision Credit: Getty

The official has taken charge of three previous matches this summer, having also officiated at the 2022 finals as well as Euro 2020 and Euro 2024.

His first big decision of the final came after 15 minutes at the MetLife Stadium.

It followed a reckless lunge from Argentina midfielder Alexis Mac Allister on Dani Olmo.



His heavy challenge did not win the ball, with Olmo left in agony on the floor.

Spain frustration

Mac Allister's attempted tackle was awarded as a foul by Vincic, with a free-kick given to Spain.



However, despite a furious reaction from their technical area, a yellow card was not shown.

Every member of the coaching staff had leapt to their feet following the challenge.



Meanwhile, Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni appeared to wave his hand as if to dismiss whether it was even a foul in the first place.

As for the Spain supporters, they quickly made their feelings on the decision known.

Chants of 'Infantino' could be heard inside the MetLife Stadium as a reference to the belief Argentina were receiving preferential treatment from the referee - a conspiracy which has dominated the World Cup.

4 Mac Allister enraged the Spain bench with a reckless lunge on Olmo after 15 minutes Credit: Getty



Another cynical challenge from Nicolas Tagliafico on Lamine Yamal was not enough to see the referee go into his pocket.

The first yellow card was eventually brandished for a late scissor challenge from Argentina's Lisandro Martinez.

Controversial decisions

It comes after controversial VAR decisions went in their favour earlier in the tournament.

Egypt saw a goal disallowed for a contentious foul in the round of 16 which would have seen them go 2-0 up.



Although they later added a second, the African side were ultimately beaten 3-2 following a late Argentina fight back.

The winning goal itself also came after penalty claims for Egypt seconds before Enzo Fernandez found the net.

4 Vincic opted not to show a yellow card to Mac Allister for his foul on Olmo Credit: AFP

Manager Hossam Hassan was left furious with the referee, launching into a post-match rant aimed at FIFA.



Meanwhile, Switzerland forward Breel Embolo was sent off after a VAR review into 'mistaken identity' in the quarter-finals.

His side were reduced to 10 men just moments after equalising.

The rare application of the protocol caused further criticism, with Argentina going on to win 3-1 after extra-time.

4 Fernandez's red card in the World Cup final provided a sense of 'karma' for England fans Credit: Getty

However, Vincic later did brandish his cards - with Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez sent off for two yellow cards during the second-half.



And it proved extremely costly for Argentina, with Spain making their man advantage count in extra-time by securing a 1-0 victory.

Sports.title: Thousands of Spain fans descend on New York City for all-night party after nail-biting World Cup final as cops crack down on chaos
Sports.content:
Thousands of Spain fans descend on New York City for all-night party after nail-biting World Cup final as cops crack down on chaos

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

New York's Times Square was taken over by thousands of jubilant Spain fans on Sunday, who partied through the night after their team's World Cup final success.

The iconic Big Apple landmark transformed into a sea of red and yellow - hours after Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the final - as fans swarmed to Midtown Manhattan.

Thousands of supporters were seen singing, dancing, chanting and waving Spanish flags as they took over Times Square from dusk until the early hours of Monday.

Many of the fans had attended a public watch party in the area, while thousands of others flocked from across the city - and MetLife Stadium itself - to celebrate.

It marked a stark contrast to how Times Square had looked just 24 hours earlier, when a myriad of Argentina fans gathered to start the festivities ahead of the game.

On Sunday, however, only a handful of La Albiceleste fans were seen in the area and - those who were there - appeared dejected, deflated and downbeat after their loss.

Times Square was full of Spain World Cup fans into the early hours of Monday morning

The iconic New York landmark was taken over by supporters of La Roja after their historic win

Fans were seen singing, dancing and waving Spanish flags as they celebrated the result

New York's iconic Empire State Building was lit up in red and yellow after Spain's win

Though spirits were high among Spain fans, New York police were forced to make several arrests - with a handful of individuals seen being placed in handcuffs by officers.

Details of the arrests have not yet been released by New York police. An NYPD spokesperson told The Daily Mail late Sunday night that the total number of arrests was unknown because the suspects were still being processed.

As for the crimes, the NYPD spokesperson said the suspects are accused of disorderly conduct.

In one exclusive photo, a Spain fan wearing a Lamine Yamal jersey is seen being led away by two officers. Another man in a pink t-shirt and matching shorts was also apprehended, as was a shirtless man seen in a video on Instagram.

However, while the party ended early for those fans, other Spain supporters were seen raising replica trophies, blowing horns and crowd surfing in the wake of the country's second World Cup win.

Meanwhile, in lower Manhattan, red-clad revelers took over the city's High Line, which is a park raised on an old rail line 30 feet above the city streets.

But Sunday's most hectic scene was Times Square, which had been a beehive of activity throughout the tournament.

Fans who couldn't afford four-figure ticket prices had dozens of watch parties to choose from throughout the five boroughs, but no option proved as popular as Times Square's seemingly endless array of towering electronic billboards.

No option proved as popular as Times Square for Spanish fans to celebrate their triumph

Despite the jubilant scenes, a number of individuals were arrested by New York police Sunday. Details of the numerous arrests in Times Square were not made immediately clear.

As pictured by The Daily Mail's John Taggart, several individuals were placed in riot cuffs

New York Police Department officers stand guard as fans gather in Times Square

Times Square has been a hive of activity throughout the World Cup, despite the fact that local tournament games such as Sunday's final were actually played at MetLife Stadium

And on Sunday, Times Square appeared to lean heavily in favor of the defending-champion Argentinians, at least before the match.

'We came across a few Spaniards but I don't look at them,' the blue-and-white-clad Florencia Luzinin, 30, told the AFP.

Afterwards, many of those Argentina fans appeared devastated, regardless of whether or not they actually claimed Argentinian citizenship.

While America does have Spanish and Argentinian immigrants, those diasporas are far smaller than others in the country, which may have led Sunday's turnout to be slightly smaller than some of the tournament's previous matches.

'It's been slightly overshadowed,' Howie Ray, 42, told the AFP. 'I think there was fatigue after all the games of the group stage and then the US getting eliminated. Spain and Argentina are also relatively small immigrant populations.

'You also have the regular folks leave for the weekend during the summer.'

Many visitors from Spain and Argentina did cross the Atlantic for the World Cup, but rather than pack into Times Square, they decided to splurge on tickets.

'Money comes back,' Buenos Aires resident Manuel Lopez Maccotta told The Associated Press. 'This is once in a lifetime. You´re seeing the best player in the world [Lionel Messi] in his last World Cup. Money is worthless compared to this.'

The Spanish festivities in Times Square began immediately after the final whistle went

Many Team Argentina fans in New York City were left devastated by Sunday's loss to Spain

A devastated Argentina fan is seen sulking on Sunday in New York's Times Square

And how much did he pay?

'Almost 10K in American money,' said Maccotta, whose friend got off relatively easy with a $5,000 ticket.

'I bought the ticket before the World Cup final,' Santiago Burcaco told the AP.

Argentina and Spain fans were comrades in this struggle.

Madrid's Curro Sanchez spent $8,000 on his ticket, and will now be staying in the city through Thursday.

'Had a big, big, big fight with my wife,' Sanchez told the AP. 'At the end of the day, she understood.'

Sports.title: Spain 1-0 Argentina: Ferran Torres' extra time winner secures World Cup trophy for Luis de la Fuente's side - as Lionel Messi suffers tournament heartbreak
Sports.content:
The voice of Frank Sinatra rang around the MetLife Stadium before the World Cup final. As he sang about facing the ‘final curtain’, the big screen showed footage of Lionel Messi holding aloft the World Cup in Qatar four years ago and being borne shoulder-high by his teammates in triumph. ‘I did it my way,’ Sinatra sang, as the Manhattan skyscrapers shimmered in the distance.

In times when football has lost itself, when it has moved away from those who love it, when it has become enslaved to money and ruled by high ticket prices, when it is led by sycophants and grifters, when it has been assailed by doubts about its integrity and its direction, Messi has always been there to redeem it, doing it his way.

This time, in the midst of this drab, angry, bitter, attritional final, doing it his way was not enough. This time, he could not redeem even his own team, who behaved with a despicable lack of grace and barely contained thuggery after the final whistle and who were utterly outclassed by Spain. Spain only won 1-0. It should have been many more.

At a World Cup afflicted by a myriad of controversies, a World Cup with a final saddled with a dirge of a half-time show and hydration breaks that are advertising breaks and President Trump calling Gianni Infantino to lobby, successfully, for Folarin Balogun’s suspension to be lifted, and $1m pitchside seats, seeing Messi play was always enough to make the heart sing.

Even at 39, the greatest player the world has ever seen, has still been the sport’s human shield. Even as Trump and Infantino have danced around the tournament like puppeteers, Messi has worked his magic, scored more goals than anyone apart from Kylian Mbappe and floated above the storms.

Spain have won the World Cup after Ferran Torres' extra time winner against Argentina

Torres smashed in the winner with his left foot after Nico Williams headed the ball back across goal

It was elation for the Spanish players as they celebrated wildly in the corner of the stadium

But it was devastation for Argentina's crestfallen stars, who had fought for their lives

Messi has graced his sport for more than 20 years and Argentina’s obstinate, defiant, sometimes desperate run to this World Cup final against Spain was predicated around this being ‘Leo’s last one’. They wanted to do it for him. They wanted to give him the send-off he deserved before he retreated to what remains of his club career with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.

And so Messi went to the well one last time in the blazing sunshine in New Jersey. Fifteen of his 21 tournament goals have come since his 35th birthday and even though Mbappe had moved ahead of him in the race for the Golden Boot on Saturday evening and ahead of him in the all-time World Cup list, many hoped Messi would put that right on Sunday, too.

The truth is that when Messi went to the well this time, the well was empty. This was a game too far, even for him. Tom Cruise had given a speech on the pitch before kick-off and this match turned into Messi’s mission impossible.

He was swallowed up in the mediocrity of a final that was at odds with so much of the drama that this World Cup has provided. It was dull and attritional. It was dominated by Spain, who finally turned their advantage into a winning goal in the second period of extra time.

And if many wanted Messi to win, by then not many wanted Argentina to win. They played with a mixture of unabashed thuggery and a desperate lack of ambition. They did not have a single shot in normal time, let alone a shot on target. If there was a shred of satisfaction about their defrocking, it was that it came with an overdue red card for Enzo Fernandez, their self-styled enforcer, at the end of normal time.

So Messi’s final fling fell flat. He did not end the competition with the Golden Boot, he did not win the second World Cup he craved, and he left the international stage after being able to exert precious little influence on his final match. Sport is no respecter of reputation.

Torres' goal sparked jubilation for the thousands of Spanish fans inside the stadium

Argentina keeper Emiliano Martinez had been in inspired form before that to keep Spain at bay

There was no fairytale World Cup ending for Lionel Messi who struggled to assert his authority

Enzo Fernandez was sent off at the end of normal time for a reckless second bookable offence

A melee ensued and Messi tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off for covering his mouth

Much of the talk before the game had been about a passing of the torch from Messi to Spain’s superstar teenager Lamine Yamal but even if Yamal had more influence than Messi, he has been struggling with the after-effects of a hamstring injury and could not stamp his brilliance on the game.

It was Ferran Torres who made the difference when he came on, Ferran Torres who scored the winner and Ferran Torres who thought he had scored a second before it was ruled out for offside. This was Spain’s second World Cup triumph after 2010. They only conceded one goal in the entire competition. They were the better team by a large margin here.

Yamal had the first chance of the game within the opening five minutes. A neat touch from Dani Olmo played Yamal in behind the Argentina defence but he did not hit his shot with enough power or accuracy to beat Emiliano Martinez.

Argentina had not started the game with the same furious intent they showed against England in the semi-final. Not driven by the same visceral resentment, they showed Spain far more respect and allowed them to dictate the tempo of the game.

Spain had only conceded one goal in the tournament before this game but they had a scare early on when Messi raced on to a through ball. He was clean through but Unai Simon sprinted 35 yards out of his goal to clear it and got there just ahead of Argentina’s skipper. Some felt Messi had missed an opportunity. ‘He had to put his body in and he didn't,' Wayne Rooney said.

Alexis Mac Allister scythed down Olmo after 15 minutes but, inexplicably, referee Slavko Vincic, chose not to show him even a yellow card. The Spain fans were infuriated. They are keenly aware of the lenient treatment Argentina have benefited from in this World Cup. ‘Infantino, Infantino,’ they jeered.

Argentina did their best to rile up Spain and there were several flashpoints between the players

Things escalated at full-time when Leandro Paredes clashed with several Spain players

The stands were filled with celebrities, including David Beckham and Tom Cruise (centre)

President Donald Trump also watched on alongside FIFA President Gianni Infantino

The pair later presented the players with their medals and handed over the trophy to Spain

Justin Bieber headlined the strange half-time show, which lasted for almost half an hour

The game settled into a kind of stalemate, the antithesis of the Soccer Aid vibe that permeated England’s third-place play-off game with France the previous day. There was, at least, a ripple of surprise when the referee booked Lisandro Martinez. It was just about the only decision that had gone Spain’s way all afternoon.

The half-time show came and went in a splurge of underwhelming banality. It was much like the opening 45 minutes, in which Argentina had not managed a single shot on target. Leandro Paredes came on at the interval and was booked within a few minutes for a shove in the back of Max Baena.

Yamal made one burst to the byline midway through the second half and cut the ball back for substitute Ferran Torres. Torres leapt well on the edge of the six-yard box but could only direct his header straight at a grateful Emiliano Martinez.

As the game approached extra time, Argentina imploded. More particularly, Enzo Fernandez imploded. Already on a yellow card, he launched himself into a tackle on Pau Cubarsi and caught the defender’s trailing foot. Cubarsi cart-wheeled into the air and Fernandez was shown a second yellow. It felt like a little karma for the rough-house tactics he had inflicted on England in Atlanta and for which he had escaped without punishment.

Increasingly, only Emiliano Martinez kept Argentina in the game. He saved well from a Yamal free kick and then, early in extra time, from a glancing header by Nico Williams. Spain thought they had scored when Martinez spilled the ball under a challenge but VAR ruled that he had been fouled. It felt like another generous decision towards Argentina.

Spain missed the best chance of the match when Arsenal’s Mikel Merino glanced a header wide from close range near the end of the first half of extra time but they finally broke the deadlock after 106 minutes when Williams nodded the ball back to Torres and Torres smashed the ball past Emiliano Martinez.

Their victory was to be celebrated. Messi’s retreat into the twilight was much to be mourned.

Sports.title: Donald Trump ignores FIFA president's call to leave the stage as he joins Spain's World Cup final trophy lift in awkward moment
Sports.content:
US President Donald Trump took center stage at MetLife Stadium on Sunday as he awkwardly invaded Spain's iconic trophy lift at the end of the FIFA World Cup final.

The European outfit clinched their second World Cup title after beating Lionel Messi's Argentina 1-0 in extra time, following a late strike from forward Ferran Torres.

Shortly after the full-time whistle, the US President made his way down to the field, where he was loudly booed by the crowd before making his way onto the stage alongside FIFA chief Gianni Infantino.

Trump and Infantino handed out various awards to match officials and players, before officially welcoming Spain's players up to the stage to lift the World Cup trophy.

The US President presented the prestigious title to Spain captain Rodri, who took great pleasure in raising it aloft in East Rutherford.

Much like when he presented the Club World Cup title last summer, Trump stood awkwardly alongside the Spain squad as they lifted the trophy and celebrated wildly.

Donald Trump took center stage as Spain lifted the World Cup trophy on Sunday afternoon

The President, along with FIFA chief Gianni Infantino, presented the trophy to Spain's Rodri

It appeared as though Infantino attempted to usher Trump away - but the President remained

It seemed as though, when Spain were about to perform the trophy lift, Infantino had attempted to usher Trump away from the players - though the President remained.

He stood to the side of the squad as the confetti cannons went off at MetLife Stadium, clapping and grinning while Infantino laughed off Trump's awkward cameo.

There were an estimated 1.5-1.8 billion viewers tuning in to watch the summer tournament's showpiece finale, where Trump and Infantino took center stage once again.

Loud boos had come from the stands when Infantino and Trump made their way onto the pitch, as fans made their feelings on the duo undoubtedly clear.

Prior to the official trophy lift, Trump also handed out silver medals to Argentina's players - including Lionel Messi - after their heartbreaking defeat in New Jersey.

Fans noted that one Argentina star - Tottenham defender Cristian Romero - completely ignored the President as he collected his medal from Infantino.

In a video which swiftly went viral on social media, the Argentinian could be seen receiving his silverware from the FIFA chief before waltzing past Trump on stage.

Meanwhile, Trump also presented a trio of awards to Spain's stars; including the Young Player of the Tournament, the Golden Glove and the Golden Ball - which were claimed by Pau Cubarsi, Unai Simon and Rodri respectively.

Trump and Infantino stood on stage as golden confetti rained down around them in New Jersey

The US President welcomed Spain's stars onto the stage before presenting the prestigious title

The President also handed out silver medals to Lionel Messi and Argentina after their loss

Trump pictured presenting Lamine Yamal with his medal after the 1-0 win at MetLife Stadium

Argentina defender Cristian Romero appeared to ignore Trump as he walked on stage

There was a degree of irony in regards to Trump presenting Spain with the World Cup trophy, after previously launching a stinging attack on the country at a UN summit earlier in July for not contributing enough money to NATO.

'Spain is a terrible partner in NATO. They don’t participate. They don’t pay. I don’t want anything to do with Spain. Cut off all trade with Spain, please, including visits,' he said. 'Don’t even talk to them. They’re hopeless, bad people.'

Then, on his way back to the United States on Air Force One, Trump said Spain had tried to improve their standings with him.

'I did have issues, and ​I still do. But Spain, they came back all the way today. Spain was very generous today,' he said.

'They honoured a request for lots of payments, and if they didn't, we wouldn't have even ⁠talked to them.'

Earlier in the day, Trump and his wife Melania were seen taking in the action inside a packed MetLife Stadium suite - alongside FIFA President Infantino, Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Trump also shook hands with Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez as Infantino stood beside them.

Spain's Queen Letizia and King Felipe VI also greeted the president. Javier Milei, the president of Argentina, is watching the game from home due to 'superstition,' The New York Times reported.

Trump cozied up to FIFA President Gianni Infantino in the private suite on Sunday afternoon in New Jersey

Inside the private suite, Infantino posed for pictures with the president's son, Eric Trump, his wife, Lara, and their children

President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania joined the massive crowd at MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon for the 2026 World Cup final match

The commander-in-chief also waved at the crowd from behind the glass.

Inside the private suite, Infantino posed for pictures with the president's son, Eric Trump, his wife, Lara, and their children. Barron Trump also showed up for the big game.

Ahead of the match, Trump told Fox News' Jenny Taft on the FIFA Red Carpet that 'it's hard to bet against Messi,' speaking of Argentina's 39-year-old star.

However, in the end, it wasn't to be for the veteran soccer star after he and Argentina came up short in their battle against European outfit Spain in East Rutherford.

The match was decided by a ferocious, close-range strike from Spanish star Ferran Torres in the 106th minute, after a 0-0 stalemate at the end of regulation time.

However, there were ugly scenes once the full-time whistle blew - with a number of frustrated Argentina stars taking out their anger on Spain's players after their loss.

After the whistle, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Lionel Messi's bid for back-to-back World Cup titles ended in failure after their loss to Spain

Several stars clashed after Spain's 1-0 win over Argentina - but the South Americans started it

Argentina's Leandro Paredes was sent off after the whistle for getting violent with Spain

Micah Richards said of their behaviour on the BBC: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, and the first of those only came in the 117th minute.

By contrast, they committed 24 fouls - though Spain didn't have clean hands themselves, as they gave away 21.

Elsewhere on the day, World Cup fans branded FIFA's controversial first-ever World Cup halftime show starring Madonna and Justin Bieber a 'disaster' on Sunday.

The futuristic segment began with Madonna, 67, singing her 2000 hit Music, accompanied by giddy Brazilian World Cup legends Ronaldo Nazario and Ronaldinho.

The toned music legend was dressed head-to-toe in Saint Laurent, wowing in a pink satin teddy jacket and corset, mini shorts and lace-up boots, paired with stockings as she embraced the soccer icons, before they drove her out into the stadium.

The unlikely trio then posed up on the grass and smiled at the crowds.

Madonna and Justin Bieber's performances during the World Cup halftime show divided fans

Shakira showed off her toned frame as she performed her hit Dai Dai with Burna Boy

Justin Bieber made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with only a guitar to sing a World Cup-themed version of his song Everything Hallelujah - leaving fans baffled

Bieber, 32, made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with nothing but a guitar to sing a World Cup themed version of his song, Everything Hallelujah.

The singer was bizarrely subbed onto the pitch by Jason Sudeikis, playing his manager alter-ego Ted Lasso.

The star looked relaxed as he casually walked onto the pitch before belting out his hit track, adding the final line, 'it's the World Cup, Hallelujah' - with fans left baffled by his song choice.

Shakira returned to the World Cup stage as she flaunted her toned abs in a pink and yellow sequined bodysuit to perform her hit Dai Dai, with Burna Boy, while K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite.

As well as a halftime show, the World Cup final also included a closing ceremony that featured performances and appearances from Post Malone, Tom Cruise, Nicole Scherzinger, influencer IShowSpeed, Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson, Robbie Williams and Italian singer Laura Pausini.

Sports.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino heads into Spain's locker room to hand out Super Bowl-style gold rings to World Cup champions
Sports.content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino wasted no time in delivering the inaugural Super Bowl-style gold rings to World Cup champions Spain shortly after their dramatic final win.

On Sunday afternoon, Spain triumphed 1-0 over Lionel Messi's Argentina in extra time after a 106th-minute strike from forward Ferran Torres at MetLife Stadium.

Ahead of the final, FIFA had revealed that it had manufactured 'bespoke championship rings', 30 of which will be presented to the winner in New Jersey.

Infantino delivered on his promise almost immediately after the match was over and was pictured handing over one of the rings to Spain captain Rodri.

The FIFA chief was seen inside Spain's locker room alongside the midfielder, who proudly accepted the ring before putting it on and snapping a picture with Infantino.

A number of Spain's stars - including the likes of Lamine Yamal and Pedro Porro - also posed with Infantino as he also provided them with replica World Cup trophies.

Infantino, pictured with Lamine Yamal, also distributed replica World Cup trophies to players

A close-up shot of the World Cup rings handed out to Spain's stars on Sunday evening

Before the final, FIFA claimed that the rings will feature an image of the golden World Cup trophy on one side, while the other will be customized after the final to 'reflect the identity of the winning team'. The details for Spain's ring are still unknown.

2,026 rings have been made in total, with 1,996 of those set to be put on sale for fans to purchase, though they are reported to be on sale for $148,000 (£110,000).

Winners' rings are a tradition in American sport. The team which reigns victorious at the Super Bowl each year are presented with typically rose gold diamond rings featuring the phrase 'World Champions'.

FIFA said today: 'One side of the ring proudly features the FIFA World Cup trophy, while the other will be customized to reflect the identity of the winning team.

'Each ring will be individually numbered, custom-fitted and delivered with its own certificate of authenticity.

'Immediately after the final, the captain and head coach of the winning team will receive temporary rings to commemorate the occasion.

'Each of the 30 rings for the winners will then be customized before being officially presented at a later date, ensuring the perfect lifelong fit for an achievement that will echo through eternity.'

Sports.title: World Cup fans brand FIFA's first-ever halftime show a 'disaster' as Madonna and Bieber's bizarre spectacle divides billions
Sports.content:
Have you got a story? Email tips@dailymail.com

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Cup fans branded FIFA's controversial first-ever World Cup halftime show starring Madonna and Justin Bieber a 'disaster' on Sunday - as the spectacle divided viewers around the world.

Argentina and Spain superstars Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal were forced to share the stage on Sunday at MetLife Stadium as the Super Bowl-inspired performance got underway - before Spain triumphed 1-0 over Argentina in extra time.

The futuristic segment began with Madonna, 67, singing her 2000 hit Music, accompanied by giddy Brazilian World Cup legends Ronaldo Nazario and Ronaldinho.

The toned music legend was dressed head-to-toe in Saint Laurent, wowing in a pink satin teddy jacket and corset, mini shorts and lace-up boots, paired with stockings as she embraced the soccer icons, before they drove her out into the stadium.

The unlikely trio then posed up on the grass and smiled at the crowds.

Bieber, 32, made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with nothing but a guitar to sing a World Cup themed version of his song, Everything Hallelujah.

The singer was bizarrely subbed onto the pitch by Jason Sudeikis, playing his manager alter-ego Ted Lasso.

Madonna and Justin Bieber's performances during the controversial first-ever FIFA World Cup halftime show divided fans on Sunday

Justin Bieber made a starkly different impact on the crowd as he stepped out with only a guitar to sing a World Cup-themed version of his song Everything Hallelujah - leaving fans baffled

Shakira showed off her toned frame as she performed her hit Dai Dai with Burna Boy

The star looked relaxed as he casually walked onto the pitch before belting out his hit track, adding the final line, 'it's the World Cup, Hallelujah' - with fans left baffled by his song choice.

One fan gave the damning verdict, 'What a disaster this halftime show was. Pre-recorded stuff, no collaborations or surprising moments. Where was Madonna at the end? She could have sung a few lines with Shakira... everything was so weird. So much hype for nothing.'

Yet making clear the division, a second viewer wrote, 'I dislike a lot of things that FIFA does... but THAT halftime show was pretty spectacular.'

Another wrote, 'Who was behind the concept for that haltfime show? Chat GPT?'

Other fans wrote, 'Madonna’s performance was the strangest thing ever, especially followed by the Muppets. The rest of the show was decent. I thought JB’s performance was the best of them all.'

'Light, bright, positive energy. We needed that. Really tired of dark and angry performances.

'It seemed like bieber was off the flow but when Shakira came up after - it all made sense!!!'

'It was great! International and diverse, a positive message, family friendly, and soccer legends hanging with Madonna! Ronaldinho and Ronaldo probably couldn't believe it!'

Bieber's downbeat song choice was undoubtedly one of the major talking points of the performance, with one fan writing, 'Justin Bieber was unfortunately the worst part of the World Cup halftime show.'

Another penned, 'Justin Bieber Hallelujah but this was not the right song choice for the half time show.'

A third typed, 'Buzz killer. Totally sucked . Why choose that song that nobody knows . Beyond me ….' while another wrote, 'terrible song choice.'

Others praised Bieber's performance, writing, 'Justin Bieber looked and sounded great at the World Cup halftime show today!

'Glad he's cleaned up his act!

'Best performance. He knows how to switch people’s moods in a second. That’s extremely difficult to do, most performers couldn’t.'

Shakira returned to the World Cup stage as she flaunted her toned abs in a pink and yellow sequined bodysuit to perform her hit Dai Dai, with Burna Boy, while K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite.

Spain eventually triumphed over Argentina 1-0 after a thrilling 30 minutes of extra time - seen with Trump at the trophy ceremony

The toned music legend showed off her legs in stockings as she embraced the soccer icons, before they drove her out into the stadium

The trio posed up on the pitch as Madonna pulled off another flawless performance

The singer was bizarrely subbed onto the pitch by Jason Sudeikis playing manager Ted Lasso

Others blasted the show over pitchy vocals and lipsync allegations

Fans slammed Bieber for his song choice on sport's biggest stage

One fan branded Bieber the 'worst part' of the show

Others praised Bieber's performance as 'so good' and worthy of the Super Bowl

K-pop sensations BTS regaled the crowd with Dynamite

BTS captivated the crowds as they continued their return to the stage after military training

The show delivered a spectacular mix of music, nostalgia and global star power, including a cameo from The Muppets

The stadium was lit up with a colorful globe and the world LOVE

[IMG 320818273 noborder /] Fans had wildly differing opinions on the spectacular

Former England star Wayne Rooney savaged the controversial World Cup final halftime show, quipping the best part of it was 'when it finished'

Liam Gallagher savaged 'This is like a bad trip', before adding: 'It's a good job I've got my spiritual socks on or that halftime entertainment could have tipped me over the edge'

The show was also blasted by former World Cup England star Wayne Rooney, 41, who joked his favorite part of the show was 'when it finished'.

'To be honest mine was when it finished I like a lot of those artists but to be honest I thought it was c**p', he fumed.

'I did honestly. It just didn't get me going, I wanted the football to be back on. It was a bit flat. I like Burna Boy I like Shakira I like Bieber but that was too flat.'

Fans were left in hysterics by Rooney's comment, with one user on X laughing: 'Wayne Rooney on the halftime show actually made me LOL and then 'I like a lot of the artists, but I thought it was c**p'.

While Liam Gallagher savaged 'This is like a bad trip', before adding: 'It's a good job I've got my spiritual socks on or that halftime entertainment could have tipped me over the edge'.

As well as a halftime show, the World Cup final also included a closing ceremony that featured performances and appearances from Post Malone, Tom Cruise, Nicole Scherzinger, influencer IShowSpeed, Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson, Robbie Williams and Italian singer Laura Pausini.

Stars including Cruise, Timothee Chalamet, Kylie Jenner, Matt Damon and Adrien Brody joined the crowds for the final.

Spanish actor Javier Bardem, skiing legend Lindsey Vonn and actress Julia Garner were also in attendance for the FIFA Gold Carpet event ahead of the final.

England icon John Terry and Argentina legend Diego Simeone were in attendance

Spain triumphed over Messi's Argentina 1-0 - after a fraught second half which saw the teams play into 30 mins of extra time.

Ferran Torres netted the winning goal in the 106th minute - with a devastated Messi watching on as his World Cup career ended in heartbreak.

World Cup final day got off to a chaotic start at MetLife Stadium with fans forced to wait for hours outside of the venue amid reports of technological glitches scanning tickets and security staff unsure of how to manage the crowds.

The attendance of President Donald Trump meant that airport-style security measures were also being enforced for everyone making their way inside of the venue.

The game was set to be the most expensive to attend in the history of sport - on Sunday morning, the cheapest ticket available on most resale websites was starting at around $7,000.

FIFA encouraged fans to arrive early in order to participate in the World Cup closing ceremony, scheduled to begin around 90 minutes before the game itself kicks off.

But it is standard procedure for fans to arrive early for additional security checks whenever Trump attends a sporting event - and he has made it to plenty in his second term as President, ranging from the Ryder Cup to the Super Bowl.

Post Malone performed ahead of the final

Cruise kept his look casual in a black tee and jeans as he posed for selfies with queuing fans, while flanked by bodyguards

The star looked excited ahead of the final

Robbie Williams, Nicole Scherzinger and Laura Pausini performed Desire

Extra security checks were in place ahead of the attendance of President Trump for the game
